summary: Join our comprehensive course on Cost-Benefit Analysis of Social Protection Programs and learn to assess the effectiveness and efficiency of social policies.
lede: Cost-benefit analysis of social protection programs helps professionals compare program costs with financial and social outcomes. For managers, program officers and analysts designing, financing or evaluating assistance, it supports identifying direct and hidden costs, assessing measurable and harder-to-value benefits, and comparing options by coverage, equity and risk. Participants also learn to explain assumptions and trade-offs when recommending allocations or reforms.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who regularly weigh costs and benefits when designing, financing, or evaluating social protection programs.
audience: M&E and results-based management specialists in social
Economists and social policy advisors in government
Social protection officers in UN agencies
modules: Principles of Cost-Benefit Thinking in Social Protection
Identifying and Classifying Costs in Social Protection Programs
Estimating and Valuing Benefits of Social Protection
Comparing Program Options and Calculating Net Benefit
Applying CBA to Key Social Protection Decisions
Building the Social Protection Investment Case
CBA in Donor-Funded and Public Sector Social Protection Portfolios
Biases and Pitfalls in Financial and Policy Judgement
CBA and Risk Management in Social Protection
Communicating and Defending Social Protection Decisions
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of social protection programs and some experience in policy analysis or program management. Familiarity with economic concepts is beneficial but not required.
